name: Door Hardware & Locks
tagline: Locks, closers and hinges — security you specify by grade
description: Door hardware is bought on brand and judged on cycles. A main-door lock is a security decision, a closer is a safety one, and a floor spring is a structural one that must be set before the flooring goes down. Each entry lists the grade or rating that actually matters.

materials.name: Main door lock
materials.blurb: Multi-point or heavy mortise lock for the entrance
materials.description: The entrance deserves a different grade from every other door: hardened bolts, an anti-drill cylinder and ideally multi-point throw. Match the backset to the door stile before ordering.

materials.name: Mortise lock
materials.blurb: Lock body housed inside the door edge — the internal standard
materials.description: A steel body mortised into the leaf, with separate handle and cylinder. Needs a solid-core door; on a hollow-core leaf the lock will pull out within a couple of years.

materials.name: Digital lock
materials.blurb: PIN, card and fingerprint entry with a mechanical override
materials.description: Keyless entry that suits families juggling keys and short-let apartments. Always confirm there is a mechanical key override and check the battery warning behaviour before specifying.

materials.name: Smart lock
materials.blurb: App-controlled entry with remote access and audit trail
materials.description: Adds Wi-Fi or Bluetooth to a digital lock: remote unlocking, temporary guest codes and a log of who entered when. Useful for rentals; check what happens when the internet drops.

specs.Features: Remote unlock, guest codes, audit log

materials.name: Door handle
materials.blurb: Lever or pull handle on a rose or plate
materials.description: Levers are easier than knobs for children and older users, and they are required for accessible design. Match the finish across the whole floor — mixed finishes read as an afterthought.

specs.Type: Lever on rose / plate, pull handle

materials.name: Door closer
materials.blurb: Controlled self-closing for fire and main doors
materials.description: Overhead or concealed, with adjustable closing and latching speeds. Mandatory on fire doors, and worth having on any door that must not be left open — size it to the leaf width and weight.

materials.name: Floor spring
materials.blurb: Concealed pivot and closer set into the floor
materials.description: Carries the weight of a heavy glass or timber door and closes it, with nothing visible above the floor. The pocket has to be cast or cut before flooring — a late decision here is expensive.

materials.name: Door stopper
materials.blurb: Floor, wall or magnetic stop that saves the wall
materials.description: Small, cheap and constantly forgotten until a handle punches a hole in the plaster. Magnetic catches also hold a door open, which helps in ventilated corridors.

materials.name: Patch fitting
materials.blurb: Corner clamps that carry frameless glass doors
materials.description: Machined clamps at the top and bottom corners of a toughened glass leaf, working with a floor spring. All cut-outs must be made before the glass is toughened.

materials.name: Door hinge (butt)
materials.blurb: Standard hinges, sized by door weight and rated in cycles
materials.description: Three hinges minimum on a solid door, four on a heavy or fire-rated one. Ball-bearing hinges last far longer under a closer; plain hinges will start to squeak and sag.

materials.name: Sliding door hardware
materials.blurb: Track, rollers and soft-close for sliding leaves
materials.description: The kit that decides whether a sliding door glides or grinds: track section, roller bearings, anti-jump guides and a soft-close damper, all rated to the leaf weight.
